public_rationale: In his 8 April 2026 post, Zitron reports on his own search. He says he does not 'see much evidence' of Anthropic custom integrations that 'actually matter'. He also says that, despite looking, he does not see 'real examples' of businesses using Claude, only announcements of 'vague partnerships'. What he saw cannot be checked from outside. Reading his words as a claim that no such examples exist would change what he said. Even that reading would depend on his own undefined tests of 'real', 'matter' and 'vague'. At least one public account of business use came before the post. On 13 February 2026, American Banker quoted Goldman Sachs' Marco Argenti describing agents built with Claude that review documents, extract entities and decide whether more documents or a separate know-your-customer check are needed (e1). The same report says 'many proofs of concept are in the works throughout Goldman' but does not say which projects these are (e2). Whether accounts like this meet his standard is his own judgment, which no one else can check. So the claim cannot be scored.
limitations: Only one dated public account, the American Banker report on Goldman Sachs, was examined. Anthropic's customer-story pages were not checked one by one for dates before the post.
The evidence does not show whether the Goldman trade accounting and onboarding agents were in production or still at the proof-of-concept stage.
The cited evidence does not show whether Zitron saw the Goldman account or any other account, or how he judged it.
The context items show that some public accounts existed. They do not show what the speaker saw or how he weighed it.

statement.excerpt: I don’t see much evidence of Anthropic creating custom integrations that actually matter, or — and fuck have I looked! — any real examples of businesses “doing stuff with Claude” other than making announcements about vague partnerships.

our_interpretation: This is a first-person report of what the speaker has found ('I don't see'). Whether he saw such evidence cannot be checked from outside.
The objective version (no public, concrete examples exist) would change his claim. Earlier reviewers flagged that change as unfair.

Even the objective version turns on his undefined standards: what counts as 'real', which integrations 'actually matter', and which announcements are 'vague'. He applies these standards strictly elsewhere in the post, for example to Goldman Sachs' detailed account.
Conclusion: not checkable as stated. Scored not_adjudicable.
criteria.support_condition: Not applicable. A first-person report of his own search, judged by his own undefined standards of 'real' and 'matter'.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Not applicable. Concrete public deployment accounts exist (see context), but whether they count as 'real examples' rather than 'vague partnerships' is his judgment to make.
